subject: Audit & access log export playbook: regional residency, TTL, and one-off snapshot questions
messages:
From: Ali Khan <ali.khan@healthops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@healthops.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on audit/access log retention, export windows and deletion proof

Hi Marissa —

We're doing a cross-team compliance check and need to confirm a few items about Redwood's audit and access logs for our production tenant. Can you please confirm the following?

1) Retention baseline for audit logs and access logs (inspector/admin events, console logins, API keys usage): default retention and whether we can extend to multi-year (7+ years) for regulatory requirements.

2) Residency options: if we choose EU residency, are exports and backups also kept within EU regions? Is there any cross-border replication by default?

3) Export capabilities: formats you provide (JSONL, Parquet, CSV), maximum time window per export, signed S3 URL delivery, manifest file with checksums, and whether you can do incremental exports for long windows.

4) Deletion workflow & proof: if we request deletion of tenant logs (end-of-contract or legal erasure), what are the exact steps, how long until physical purge, and can you provide a signed certificate or hash list proving deletion?

5) Attestation SLA: if we request a full export or deletion attestation, what is the expected turnaround SLA and any limitations for very large datasets?

If you can point me to a sample export spec or playbook (manifest format, typical file sizes, estimated costs), that would be helpful. Attaching our compliance checklist in the follow-up if needed.

Thanks,
Ali
Security & Compliance
HealthOps
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ali Khan <ali.khan@healthops.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention, export windows and deletion proof

Hi Ali —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise playbook addressing each item; I attached a short export_spec sample (log_export_spec_v1.pdf) that shows the manifest fields and a couple of example CLI/API calls. I'll loop in Karthik for the technical detail and Ben for visibility on cost/contracting.

1) Retention baseline
- Hosted (standard): audit & access logs retained for 13 months by default (rolling window).
- Enterprise add-on: configurable retention up to 7 years (subject to storage commit). We can set retention per-tenant and per-log-type (audit, access, admin).

2) Residency
- If you select EU residency at onboarding, primary storage and exports are scoped to EU regions (no cross-border replication for audit/access logs by default). Backups and export staging remain inside the region unless you request cross-region export.
- For mixed-region tenants we provide explicit mapping: tenant metadata indicates primary region for logs.

3) Export capabilities
- Formats: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), Parquet, compressed CSV.
- Delivery: signed S3 PUT/GET URLs (time-limited), or direct transfer to your SFTP endpoint.
- Windowing: exports can be sliced by day/week/month. For performance we recommend chunking >30 days into multiple files.
- Incremental exports: supported via resume tokens; we can provide delta exports for long windows to avoid full snapshots.
- Manifest: each export includes a manifest.json with file list, record counts, SHA256 checksums, and tenant+region metadata.

4) Deletion workflow & proof
- Workflow: customer initiates deletion request -> system tombstones records immediately (logical delete) -> background job physically purges data from active storage within 30–90 days depending on size and retention policies -> final archival purge occurs per compaction windows (up to 180 days in rare edge cases for very large historical dumps).
- Legal hold: any legal/GC hold will suspend purge until released.
- Proof: we provide an attestation package which includes export manifest snapshots (pre-delete), a deletion manifest (files cleared), and SHA256 fingerprints. For enterprise contracts we can provide a signed certificate (PDF) signed by our compliance team.

5) Attestation SLA & limits
- Typical turnaround: small exports (<100 GB) = 3 business days; large exports up to 2 TB = 5–10 business days (depends on chunking and scheduling).
- Deletion attestation: 7–15 business days for full proof package for large tenants. Emergency/expedited requests can be requested but will be assessed case-by-case.

Next steps: please fill out the export request form (link in the attached spec) with date ranges and preferred format. If you want we can schedule a short walkthrough of the export spec and the attestation packet.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: log_export_spec_v1.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ali Khan <ali.khan@healthops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 07:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention, export windows and deletion proof

Adding a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime/export side:

- Partitioning: logs are partitioned by tenant_id -> region -> date. This lets us slice exports efficiently and avoid cross-tenant mixing.
- Indexes & ordering: exports preserve event timestamps and include an event_id field (monotonic per-tenant) so you can re-order/consume deterministically.
- Export API: POST /v1/admin/exports with payload (tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, format=ndjson|parquet, delivery={s3,sftp}) returns an export_id. Use GET /v1/admin/exports/{export_id}/manifest to poll for manifest + signed URLs.
- Resume tokens: for very large windows we emit resume_token in the manifest which you can pass to request the next chunk (offset-based).
- Deletion internals: logical deletes mark entries as tombstoned in the write-ahead layer; compaction jobs remove tombstones and reclaim storage. Physical purges trigger object deletion from S3-compatible storage + index pruning. We retain audit logs from immutable cold archives only per your retention setting; if you request early purge we run a controlled object deletion + manifest update.
- Hashes: SHA256 is computed per-file and included in the manifest. For extra assurance we can provide a signed Merkle root for the export on request.

Ben — cost estimate: for a ~1 TB export (Parquet, EU region) we estimate ~USD 450 for transfer + listing + staging. I'll confirm exact pricing in follow-up.

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
